TryModifyPowerAmountReceived.maps_to: cmds.py:299-306, a hand-written branch inside PowerCmd.apply -- ArtifactPower itself declares no hook (powers.py:315-325)
TryModifyPowerAmountReceived.issue: The interception is reimplemented outside the hook system entirely, and the debuff test is the wrong one. C# (ArtifactPower.cs:17-36) is a TryModifyPowerAmountReceived listener whose three guards are `target != Owner`, `canonicalPower.GetTypeForAmount(amount) != Debuff`, and `!canonicalPower.IsVisible`; cmds.py:299 instead tests the applied class's static `power_cls.power_type == PowerType.DEBUFF`. That is audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G1 and its guard G3 (Artifact is not a modify_power_amount listener at all); per binding rule 3 this entry carries the identical verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued -- DORMANT in both directions, trigger = porting Malaise.cs:39 or Resonance.cs:33. Recorded here because it is THIS unit's only real behaviour and a reader of artifact.json must not be left thinking the port is hook-shaped.

AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): STALE. The record predates round 12 Task 18's AfterModifyingPowerAmount* machinery (power_cmd/G3+G4). Re-verified against today's powers.py/cmds.py: Artifact is now a real listener consuming its stack through the full ModifyAmount pipeline, matching ArtifactPower.cs:38-41 exactly. The reasoning replaced: that the stack-consumption event was hand-inlined because no such machinery existed -- it exists now.  The text it replaced read: The stack-consumption event is hand-inlined. C# consumes the stack via `PowerCmd.Decrement(this)` from AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived (ArtifactPower.cs:38-41) -- i.e. through the full ModifyAmount pipeline, which is what runs ShouldRemoveDueToAmount. The sim decrements the field and calls _expire() directly. This is audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G4 (no AfterModifyingPowerAmountGiven/Received machinery exists in the sim, and both real C# listeners -- Artifact and Ruined Helmet -- are hand-inlined instead); per rule 3 the same verdict, cross-referenced. The observable for Artifact specifically is identical, which is why power_cmd calls the inline reimplementation individually correct.

guards.rationale: The sim looks the power up on the target directly (`target.powers.get('artifact')`, cmds.py:300), so the owner scoping is structural rather than a filter. Settled as `faithful` note N3 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json -- architecturally different, semantically identical. Cross-referenced, not re-argued.

The sim has no IsVisible concept. Genuinely inert rather than merely untriggered: PowerModel.IsVisible (src/Core/Models/PowerModel.cs:150-160 -- the file sits directly under Models/, NOT under Models/Powers/) returns IsVisibleInternal, the overridable virtual at PowerModel.cs:167, for a self-or-enemy target, and EXECUTED -- `py audit/tools/power_census.py visible` -- **0 of the 260 .cs files directly under src/Core/Models/Powers override IsVisibleInternal** (260 EXCLUDES the 16 files in Powers/Mocks/; 276 including them, and a recursive grep that does cover Mocks/ also returns 0), so it is provably always true for every power in the whole decompiled game, not just the ported ones. Same finding and same verdict as power_cmd note N1. PROMPT.md bug class 4 (visibility guards) is therefore CLEAR for this unit and for every other power unit. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.what: One Artifact instance carries N stacks, so one debuff costs one stack
guards.rationale: C#'s ModifyPowerAmountReceived walks listeners, and a creature holds at most one ArtifactPower instance (Creature.cs:607 throws on a second instance of a PowerInstanceType.None power), so one application consumes exactly one stack; cmds.py:302-305 does the same. Already pinned by test/test_powers.py::TestArtifact::test_blocks_one_debuff_per_stack and ::test_stacks_and_each_stack_blocks_one_debuff, verified present by grep (binding rule 8).

guards.what: Artifact has no turn hook, so it never expires on its own
guards.rationale: C# declares no turn hook on ArtifactPower and the sim's class body is empty of hooks (powers.py:315-325). Both remove it only by stack exhaustion.
